target.title: fix: keep usage day buckets correct across DST
target.body:
Closes #103092

AI-assisted: yes — implemented and reviewed with Codex under maintainer direction.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users viewing multi-month or all-time Usage and Profile history in DST-observing time zones could see midnight-adjacent events assigned to the neighboring calendar day. This produced incorrect heatmap cells, streaks, daily totals, and peak-day results.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an optional IANA `timeZone` to the existing usage RPC parameters and uses that zone's offset at each event timestamp for both date-range boundaries and daily aggregation in `usage.cost` and `sessions.usage`. The Control UI sends the browser's IANA zone together with the existing `utcOffset`; recognized zones take precedence, while fixed-offset clients and runtimes that do not recognize a newer zone retain the existing fallback behavior.

## User Impact

Usage and Profile history now remains aligned with the user's actual local calendar across spring-forward and fall-back transitions. Existing clients that send only `utcOffset` keep their current fixed-offset behavior, and the protocol change is additive.

## Evidence

- Deterministic repro: `2026-01-31T22:30:00Z` is January 31 at 23:30 in `Europe/Vienna`; applying a summer-fixed UTC+2 offset incorrectly labels it February 1, while IANA bucketing keeps it on January 31.
- Regression coverage includes IANA schema acceptance, 23-hour and 25-hour boundaries, per-event Vienna bucketing, both usage endpoints, cache-key separation, invalid-zone handling, legacy fallback, and browser request parameters.
- Blacksmith Testbox: `tbx_01kx4742ygjemdm386m7hmf4ay` (`crimson-krill`).
- Focused tests: `corepack pnpm test packages/gateway-protocol/src/index.test.ts src/infra/format-time/format-time.test.ts src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/usage.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/usage.sessions-usage.test.ts ui/src/lib/sessions/usage.test.ts` — 303 tests passed across four shards.
